headline: Highest risk is low: both open-source, non-runnable profiles have no shared I/O or egress, so only weak interaction pathways exist.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface is documented for either data-engineering-zoomcamp or godot_rl_agents. With both profiles showing io_surfaces empty and network egress none, there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge between them.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard bridge, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw outputs as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared workspaces.
Do not route one agent's text directly into the other's prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, both have network egress set to none, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented. That makes cross-agent leakage via the pair itself unsubstantiated for both data-engineering-zoomcamp and godot_rl_agents.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, reassess exfiltration pathways.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage separation if shared storage is added.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, git state, database access, or OAuth scopes are documented for either agent. Because both profiles have empty io_surfaces and empty permissions_requested, a write-conflict pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later given write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk becomes relevant.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Neither profile is documented as producing authoritative facts for the other, and both are non-runnable course/simulation repositories rather than action-taking agents. Without a downstream action path, there is no documented cascade from data-engineering-zoomcamp into godot_rl_agents or vice versa.
conditions: IF one profile is wrapped into an automation that consumes the other's outputs as authoritative input, reassess.
IF either agent is connected to email, commits, or other side-effecting tools, cascading-error risk changes.
mitigations: Do not treat one repository's output as ground truth for the other.
Insert a human review step before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add validation checks if automation is later attached.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights obligations are documented for either open-source profile, and neither touches data classes. With no regulated data flow shown, there is no compliance mismatch to attribute to this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow, reassess compliance.
IF deployment documentation later specifies residency or retention constraints, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair's current workflows.
Document any future residency or retention requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data handling is added.
